welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the doctors of the ancient and medieval worlds — and the four humours that ruled medicine for 1,500 years.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Hippocrates lived around 460-370 BC.

He told doctors to observe symptoms carefully and let nature heal. His Four Humours theory said health meant keeping blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile in balance.

Galen (c.129-216 AD) was a Greek doctor in Rome.

He developed the theory of opposites — treat too much heat with cold. He dissected animals and got some human anatomy wrong, but his books shaped medicine for 1,500 years.

In the Middle Ages the Church taught Galen as fact.

Dissection was rare. Treatments included bloodletting, herbs, prayer and pilgrimage. The Black Death of 1348-49 killed about a third of England's people — yet doctors still blamed miasma and God.

mcqs.q: Which doctor's ideas dominated Western medicine for around 1,500 years?
options: Hippocrates
Galen
Vesalius
Pasteur

mcqs.q: How many humours did the ancient Greek theory say the body contained?
What was the theory of the four humours?
options: The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
Disease was caused by imbalance of blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile; treatment aimed to rebalance them via bloodletting, purging or diet. It dominated for nearly 2,000 years.
Medieval doctors knew about germs but used humours because they had no medicine.
Medieval people thought it was caused by germs they couldn't see.

mcqs.q: How did medieval people explain the Black Death?
options: Most blamed God's punishment for sin or bad air (miasma); some scapegoated Jews; doctors blamed planetary alignments and imbalanced humours.
Medieval people knew it was spread by rats and fleas but had no way to stop it.
The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
Medieval people thought it was caused by germs they couldn't see.

mcqs.q: Why was Vesalius significant in the history of medicine?
options: His 1543 De Humani Corporis Fabrica corrected Galen's errors via human dissection and accurate illustration, founding modern anatomy though not curing disease.
The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
Vesalius invented the microscope.
Vesalius discovered the cause of disease and ended humoral theory.
